text: +100.+ So a transitive verb describes an action which passes over from the subject to the object. As for example in the sentence, _The player struck the ball, struck_ is a transitive verb--a verb of action--describing the action of the subject, player, which passes over to the object, ball. Therefore we have our definition of a transitive verb: +A transitive verb is one that has a complement showing who or what receives the action expressed by the verb.+ +The complement or word that denotes the receiver of the action expressed by a transitive verb is called the object.+ When you look up the meaning of verbs in your dictionary, you will find some verbs marked v.i., and some verbs marked v.t. V.t. is the abbreviation for verb transitive. Whenever you find a verb marked v.t., you know that it is a transitive verb, a verb of action, one which requires an object to complete its meaning. V.i.
